item.title: Anthropic IPO Is the “One We’ve Been Waiting For”: Bessemer’s Deeter
item.description:
Bloomberg Tech • Oct 26th, 2026
Anthropic IPO Is the “One We’ve Been Waiting For”: Bessemer’s Deeter
Anthropic’s IPO will finally give public market investors a chance to get into the software side of AI, says Byron Deeter, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners. Bessemer first invested in Anthropic during its Series D, and Deeter explains the impact Anthropic going public will have on limited partners. He joins Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech”.

A revival of the artificial-intelligence trade fueled gains in stocks as Anthropic PBC filed for an IPO, with investors bracing for this week’s results from tech giants and the Federal Reserve decision.
The S&P 500 halted back-to-back losses. High-profile chipmakers rallied, sending a closely watched industry gauge up 3.5%. The Nasdaq 100 rose 1.3%. In a volatile session, Brent crude hovered near $116. Brazilian markets tumbled as President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was re-elected, fueling fears that fiscal issues in Latin America’s largest economy will worsen.

US stocks gained on Monday as investors digest Anthropic PBC’s filing for its initial public offering and look forward to key big tech earnings this week as well as the Federal Reserve’s next decision on Wednesday.
The S&P 500 Index gained 0.8% as of 2:01 p.m. in New York, while the Nasdaq 100 was up 1.4%. Brent crude fell 0.53% to $116 a barrel.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
A big swath of the riskiest borrowers have few options other than defaulting on their piling debt as it’s getting increasingly expensive to refinance, CVC Marathon Chief Executive Officer Bruce Richards warned.
Default probabilities for CCC rated borrowers assigned by rating agencies have grown to 50%-60% in the next three to five years, as rates on junk-rated debt have surged and credit spreads have widened to levels signaling distress, Richards said on Bloomberg TV Monday.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Spreads on asset backed securities funding data-center developments will continue to widen as companies rush to tap different debt markets to finance their artificial intelligence endeavors, according to Morgan Stanley strategists.
AAA data-center spreads around 200 basis points look attractive, but the consensus among investors seems to be that there will be further widening, strategists including James Egan and Carolyn Campbell wrote in an Oct. 22 note. This will also happen further down the data-center ABS capital stack, though the pace is likely to slow, they added.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
A measure of French bond risk posted its biggest drop since the 2020 pandemic as local markets rallied after the nation dodged a downgrade at Moody’s Ratings.
The extra yield investors demand to hold 10-year French bonds, known as OATs, over safer German debt fell 14 basis points to 154 basis points on Monday, the largest drop in six years on a closing basis. France’s stocks rose and the euro outperformed most of its G10 peers.

The National Basketball Association reached a deal with Kalshi and Polymarket that designates the platforms as the league’s preferred prediction market exchanges, in addition to announcing an information sharing agreement with the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
The NBA said Monday that it would license official data to the top prediction market platforms. The agreement puts in place limitations on permissible markets, information-sharing obligations for rooting out suspicious trading and prohibitions on trading by NBA league and team personnel.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Colombia is selling dollar bonds for the first time since January, as a new administration pledges to rein in the widening budget gap and put the nation’s debt back on a sustainable path.
The nation is issuingBloomberg Terminal
notes due in 2032, 2037 and 2056, with guidance for pricing around 7.1%, 7.7% and between 8.15% and 8.25%, respectively, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified. The deal comes weeks after government officials opened talks with the International Monetary Fund to discuss solutions for what they claim is the widest fiscal gap in history.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
The average price Americans are paying for gasoline under President Donald Trump has overtaken the average during the Biden administration, underscoring the political pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections.
Trump had pledged to lower gasoline prices to below $2 a gallon, but almost two years into his presidency the fuel’s retail cost has averaged $3.472 a gallon, according to the American Automobile Association. That surpassed the average under former President Joe Biden of $3.471 a gallon by less than a cent, according to daily AAA data released Monday.

item.title: Brazil Markets Crater, Some Stocks Sink 50% After Lula Victory
item.description: Brazilian markets cratered, with the currency and the benchmark stock index quickly racking up losses of more than 10%, as the surprise re-election of leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva blew up the bullish wagers that investors had made on the country in recent weeks.

item.title: CPPIB Said to Explore Sale of Stake in Spain’s Largest Gas Grid
item.description: Canada Pension Plan Investment Board is weighing a sale of its 12% stake in Spain’s largest gas distributor, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Verizon Sees Customer Surge, But Competition Fears Persist
item.description: Verizon Communications Inc. reported its strongest third-quarter performance in wireless customer additions in five years, adding a net 406,000 monthly phone lines. The company's shares were down 2.8% due to concerns about increased competition from SpaceX's forthcoming Starlink Mobile service. Bloomberg's John Butler joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Shock Lula Win Derails $6 Billion in Equity Sales as Banks Reel
item.description: Brazilian companies had some $6 billion in equity sales lined up for the weeks after the vote that they expected would crown conservative Flávio Bolsonaro as the next president of Latin America’s largest economy.

item.title: (USD:UGX) Shilling Freefall Has Uganda Tapping Meager Reserve War-Chest
item.description: Uganda’s shilling sank to a fresh low against the dollar even after the central bank tapped its reserves for the second time in a week to prop up the currency, defying a directive from President Yoweri Museveni not to use the country’s buffers for that purpose.
